race_context: The ballot's "Carroll Delphi Community School Board" is the board of the Delphi Community School Corporation (DCSC) in Carroll County, which runs four schools: Delphi Community High School, Delphi Community Middle School, Delphi Community Elementary School and Camden Early Childhood Center {dcsc_home}{in_list}. A district-wide enrollment figure was not found in fetched sources; the high school reports 417 students {dchs_profile}.
Dr. Pamela Moore became superintendent in 2025; she previously led Tri-Township Consolidated School Corporation in Wanatah {ccc_moore}{dcsc_supt}.

The board has seven members {dcsc_board}. Members are elected by district, and "only the voters of any given district elect the candidate from that district," according to a 2006 Carroll County Comet description; that article placed District 2 in Deer Creek Townships 3 and 5 and District 7 in Tippecanoe Townships 1 and 2 {ccc_districts}. Current district boundaries were not confirmed in a newer source.

Current members listed by the district are Zach Owen (president), Stephanie Mills (vice president), Kirk Schwarzkopf (secretary), Chris Nipple, Mike Priest, Gil Smith and Tim Strasser {dcsc_board}. The district lists terms ending in 2026 for Mills, Priest, Schwarzkopf and Smith {dcsc_board}; Strasser (District 4), Owen (District 5) and Nipple (District 6) were elected unopposed in 2024 {ccc_2024res}.

Two seats are on the 2026 ballot, each electing one member: District 2, held by Gil Smith (elected unopposed in 2022), and District 7, held by Mike Priest (elected 2018 and unopposed in 2022) {ccc_2022}{ccc_2018}{in_list}. Neither incumbent is on the 2026 candidate list, so both seats will have new members {inc_list}.

District 2 is contested among three candidates: Andrea R Smothers (Democratic), Kevin D Gaskill (Republican) and Pamela Minier (no party) {in_list}{inc_list}. District 7 has one candidate, Brandi Nichols Farrer (Republican) {in_list}.

Schwarzkopf won District 3 in 2018 and was unopposed in 2022 {ccc_2018}{ccc_2022}, and Mills was appointed to the District 1 seat after holdover member Steve Myer stepped down at the end of 2023 {ccc_vacancy}. The district lists both of their terms as ending in 2026, but Districts 1 and 3 do not appear on the 2026 candidate list {dcsc_board}{inc_list}; how those seats will be filled was not found in fetched sources.

Budget and taxes: in November 2022 voters rejected a DCSC referendum for a property tax to supplement the Education Fund, 1,608 (55.14%) against to 1,294 (44.59%) for {ccc_2022}. In 2026 the district posted a budget notice for public hearing, a 2027-2029 capital projects plan, a 2027-2039 bus replacement plan, a Sept. 14, 2026 notice of additional appropriations and a notice of determination to issue bonds {dcsc_home}{dcsc_budget}. No fetched source described the effect of the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) on DCSC or any 2026 referendum.

Academics: on 2025 state data, Delphi Community Elementary School had a 3rd-grade IREAD-3 pass rate of 84.1%, ILEARN English/language arts proficiency of 26.9% and ILEARN math proficiency of 35.4% {idoe_dces}.

Governance: in spring 2026 the Indiana School Boards Association recognized the DCSC board and members Zach Owen, Mike Priest, Gil Smith and Kirk Schwarzkopf with Exemplary Governance Awards {ccc_isba}.
No candidate forums or questionnaires for the DCSC races were found in fetched sources {dcsc_boardhome}.

candidates.summary: Challenger for the open District 2 seat; listed on the state ballot list as Democratic {in_list}. Spoke at DCSC board meetings as a parent in 2018 {ccc_art2018}.
background: In 2018 the Carroll County Comet described her as a district patron with a fourth-grade child in the schools {ccc_art2018}.
No information on her occupation was found in fetched sources.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the 2026 general-election ballot as Democratic for District 2 {in_list}{inc_list}.

items: In January 2018 she asked the board how elementary art classes could be brought back and suggested the corporation look for grant funding like the Delphi Public Library's visiting-artist grant {ccc_art2018}.
At an August 2018 public hearing she asked corporation leaders to find ways to fund an art teacher {ccc_contract2018}.

on_incumbent: In a July 2018 letter to the editor she questioned why administrators and the board did not value art education and urged parents to attend the August 13, 2018 board meeting on the superintendent's contract, writing, "The need for Art Education is so important." {ccc_letter2018}

items: In April 2023 she wrote in response to a DCSC administration proposal "to move two kindergarten classes from Camden to Delphi Community Elementary School," arguing that the Camden school already worked well for young children {ccc_minier_letter}.

In the same letter she questioned why Camden's existing special-needs teachers could not serve the students, writing, "Currently there are two special needs teachers employed at Camden with caseloads under 15 and under 5." {ccc_minier_letter}
She also asked how transportation for the young students would be handled and urged readers to "Attend board meetings with your thoughts." {ccc_minier_letter}
